summary: In Greek mythology, Actor (Ancient Greek Ἄκτωρ, "leader") son of Phorbas and Hyrmine is the Elean king who marries Molione and fathers the twin Moliones Cteatus and Eurytus. Homer speaks of their grandsons Amphimachus and Thalpius as "of the blood of Actor." Distinct from Actor the Argonaut, Actor son of Azeus, and other Actors.
etymology: Ancient Greek Ἄκτωρ from ἄγω, "to lead"; a very common mythic name.

sections.heading: Father of the Moliones
paragraphs: Handbook tradition makes this Actor son of Phorbas and Hyrmine, brother of Augeas, founder of Hyrmina, and husband of Molione. By her he fathers Eurytus and Cteatus — the Molionides, sometimes described as joined twins — whom Augeas appoints generals against Heracles. Pausanias records their tomb at Cleonae.

Homer never stages Actor on stage: the Catalogue and later books call Amphimachus and Thalpius men "of the blood of Actor," sons of Cteatus and Eurytus. Nestor remembers nearly slaying the twin Moliones before Poseidon shrouded them in mist.

sections.heading: Homonym care
paragraphs: The atlas id actor-epeian is the Elean father of the Moliones alone. Distinct from actor-argonaut (Hippasus' Achaean Argonaut from Pellene), actor-azeus (Minyan father of Astyoche), and the many other Actors listed on the Wikipedia disambiguation.
